faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Got questions? Here is everything you need to know about calculating YouTube playlist lengths.

items.q: How do I calculate YouTube playlist length?
items.a: Paste your YouTube playlist URL into the calculator above and click Calculate. The tool uses the YouTube Data API to fetch every video in the playlist and sum their durations to give you the exact total length in hours, minutes, and seconds.

items.q: Can I calculate watch time at 1.5x or 2x speed?
items.a: Yes. After calculating your playlist, the Speed Comparison table shows the adjusted watch time at 0.5x, 0.75x, 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, 1.75x, 2x, 2.25x, 2.5x, and 3x. You can also enter a completely custom speed like 1.3x or 2.7x.

items.q: Can I calculate only part of a playlist?
items.a: Yes. Use the "Range" mode to specify a start and end video number. For example, set Start: 10, End: 50 to calculate only videos 10 through 50. Use "Remaining" mode to calculate how much is left after a specific video.

items.q: Why are some videos missing from my results?
items.a: Some videos may be unavailable due to being private, deleted, region-restricted, or removed by the uploader. These are counted and labeled in the results, but their duration cannot be fetched via the YouTube API.

The calculation is precise — it uses the exact duration metadata from the YouTube Data API for each individual video. However, private, deleted, or unavailable videos are excluded. Live streams report 0 seconds until they end.

items.q: Does this tool store my playlist URL?
items.a: No. Your URL is used only to make a temporary request to the YouTube API. It is not stored, logged, or used for any other purpose. See our Privacy Policy for full details.

items.q: Do I need a YouTube API key?
items.a: No — the tool works without you needing to provide one. We handle API access on our server. Power users who have their own YouTube API key can optionally use it to bypass shared quota limits.

items.q: Can I calculate a single YouTube video?
items.a: Yes. Paste any YouTube video URL (youtube.com/watch?v=... or youtu.be/...) and it will return the video duration along with speed-adjusted watch times.
Yes. YT Playlist Cal is completely free, with no paid plans, no signup, and no usage limits for normal use.

howItWorksDetail.title: How the YouTube Playlist Calculator Works
howItWorksDetail.subtitle: A transparent explanation of how YT Playlist Cal fetches data, calculates durations, and handles edge cases.
howItWorksDetail.s1Detail: You paste any YouTube URL into the input — a playlist link, a video URL with a list parameter, a youtu.be link, or a raw playlist ID. The tool validates the URL format on the client side before making any request.
howItWorksDetail.s2Detail: Your browser sends the URL to our secure server endpoint. The server parses the URL to extract the playlist ID. The YouTube Data API key is stored securely in server environment variables — it is never exposed to the browser.
howItWorksDetail.s3Detail: The server calls the YouTube Data API v3 playlists.list endpoint to retrieve the playlist title, channel name, thumbnail, and total item count.
howItWorksDetail.s4Detail: The server then calls playlistItems.list, which returns up to 50 items per request. For playlists with more than 50 videos, the API is called repeatedly using page tokens until all video IDs in the requested range have been collected.
howItWorksDetail.s5Title: Video durations are fetched in batches
howItWorksDetail.s5Detail: With all video IDs collected, the server calls videos.list in batches of 50 (the maximum per request). For each video, it retrieves the ISO 8601 duration string (e.g., PT1H2M30S = 1 hour, 2 minutes, 30 seconds).
howItWorksDetail.s6Detail: The server converts each ISO duration string to seconds, sums them, and formats the total as hours, minutes, and seconds. Videos that are unavailable (private, deleted, region-restricted) are counted separately and excluded from the total.
howItWorksDetail.s7Detail: The structured result (playlist info, video list, total duration, unavailable count) is returned as JSON. The browser renders the result dashboard, speed table, video list, and watch planner tools.
howItWorksDetail.speedIntro: Adjusted watch time at a given playback speed is calculated as:
howItWorksDetail.speedExample: For example, a 10-hour playlist at 1.5× speed: 36,000 ÷ 1.5 = 24,000 seconds = 6 hours 40 minutes.
howItWorksDetail.missingIntro: The YouTube Data API cannot return information about:
howItWorksDetail.missing1: Private videos — marked private by the uploader after being added to the playlist.
howItWorksDetail.missing2: Deleted videos — removed from YouTube entirely.
howItWorksDetail.missing3: Region-restricted videos — unavailable in the server's geographic region.
howItWorksDetail.missing4: Age-restricted videos — some may require authentication to access metadata.
howItWorksDetail.missing5: Active live streams — no fixed duration until the stream ends.
howItWorksDetail.missingOutro: These videos are counted and labeled in the results so you understand exactly what was and wasn't included.
howItWorksDetail.cachingDetail: To minimize YouTube API quota usage and improve response speed, playlist results are cached for one hour on the server. Video metadata is cached for 24 hours. If you calculate the same playlist within this window, results are served from cache instantly.

faqDetailed.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqDetailed.subtitle: Everything you need to know about calculating YouTube playlist length and watch time.
faqDetailed.q1: How do I calculate YouTube playlist length?
faqDetailed.a1: Paste your YouTube playlist URL into the calculator on the homepage and click Calculate. The tool uses the YouTube Data API to retrieve every video in the playlist and sums their durations. You'll get the total length in hours, minutes, and seconds instantly.
faqDetailed.a2: All standard YouTube formats are supported: full playlist URLs (youtube.com/playlist?list=...), video URLs with a playlist parameter, youtu.be short links, plain playlist IDs (PLxxxxxx), and individual video URLs (for single-video duration).
faqDetailed.q3: Can I calculate duration for a single YouTube video?
faqDetailed.a3: Yes. Paste any YouTube video URL and the tool will return its exact duration along with a speed comparison table showing how long it would take at 0.5x through 3x speed.
faqDetailed.a4: The calculation is precise. It uses the exact duration metadata provided by the YouTube Data API for every individual video. The only exception is unavailable videos (private, deleted, region-restricted) which report 0 seconds and are excluded from the total.
faqDetailed.q5: Does the tool support private playlists?
faqDetailed.a5: No. The YouTube Data API only provides access to public and unlisted playlists. Private playlists require account authentication and cannot be calculated using this tool.
faqDetailed.q6: Can I calculate watch time at 1.5x or 2x speed?
faqDetailed.a6: Yes. After calculating your playlist, the Speed Comparison table shows watch time at 0.5×, 0.75×, 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75×, 2×, 2.25×, 2.5×, and 3×. You can also type any custom speed in the Custom Speed field.
faqDetailed.q7: How much time does 2x speed save?
faqDetailed.a7: At 2x speed, you save exactly 50% of the original watch time. A 10-hour playlist becomes 5 hours. A 20-hour course becomes 10 hours. The speed table after calculation shows the exact time saved for every preset speed.
faqDetailed.q8: What is the fastest supported speed?
faqDetailed.a8: The preset buttons go up to 3×. You can enter any custom value in the Custom Speed field, up to 5×. Note that YouTube's player itself only goes up to 2× natively — higher speeds require browser extensions or workarounds.
faqDetailed.q9: Can I calculate only part of a playlist?
faqDetailed.a9: Yes. Select the "Range" mode and enter a start and end video number. For example, Start: 10, End: 50 will calculate only videos 10 through 50. This is useful for studying specific modules of a course.
faqDetailed.a10: Select "Remaining" mode and enter the number of the last video you watched. The tool will calculate the duration of all videos after that point. For example, if you enter 12, it calculates videos 13 onwards.
faqDetailed.q11: Can I calculate multiple playlists at once?
faqDetailed.a11: Currently, the tool calculates one playlist at a time. A Playlist Comparison feature is planned for a future update.
faqDetailed.q12: Why are some videos missing from my total?
faqDetailed.a12: Some videos may be excluded because they are private (made private by the uploader), deleted from YouTube, region-restricted (unavailable in your country), or removed due to a copyright claim. These are counted and displayed in the results as "unavailable" but their duration cannot be fetched.
faqDetailed.q13: Why does my playlist show fewer videos than YouTube?
faqDetailed.a13: YouTube counts all videos in the playlist including private and deleted ones. The YouTube API only returns videos it can access. If there is a discrepancy, it typically means some videos in the playlist are private, deleted, or otherwise inaccessible to the API.
faqDetailed.q14: What happens with live streams in a playlist?
faqDetailed.a14: Live streams that are currently live have no fixed duration, so they report 0 seconds and are counted as unavailable. Once a live stream ends and YouTube processes the recording, its duration will be available on the next calculation.
faqDetailed.q15: How does the Watch Planner work?
faqDetailed.a15: After calculating your playlist, scroll down to the Daily Watch Planner section. Enter your daily watch budget (in minutes), your starting date, and your preferred speed. The planner will calculate how many days you need and your estimated finish date.
faqDetailed.q16: How does the Finish-By Calculator work?
faqDetailed.a16: The Finish-By Calculator works in reverse. Enter a target date (e.g. your exam date) and a preferred speed. The tool calculates how many minutes per day you need to watch to finish on time.
faqDetailed.q17: Can I plan around specific days of the week?
faqDetailed.a17: The current planner assumes daily viewing. Support for custom weekly schedules (e.g. weekdays only) is planned for a future update.
faqDetailed.q18: Does YT Playlist Cal store my playlist URLs?
faqDetailed.a18: No. Your URL is used only to make a temporary request to the YouTube API. It is not saved to a database, logged, or used for any purpose beyond the immediate calculation. See our Privacy Policy for full details.
faqDetailed.q19: Do I need a YouTube or Google account?
faqDetailed.a19: No. The tool works entirely without any account, login, or signup.
faqDetailed.q20: Do you require a YouTube API key?
faqDetailed.a20: No. The tool provides its own server-side YouTube API key. Power users who have exhausted the shared quota can optionally enter their own key in Advanced Options — it is only used for that request and is never stored.
faqDetailed.q21: Is my YouTube API key safe if I enter it?
faqDetailed.a21: Your key is sent to our server only for the duration of the API request. It is not logged, stored, or used for any other purpose. It is transmitted over HTTPS. We strongly recommend using a YouTube API key with appropriate quota limits.
faqDetailed.a22: Yes. YT Playlist Cal is completely free. There are no paid plans, no usage limits for normal use, and no signup required.
faqDetailed.q23: Is this tool affiliated with YouTube or Google?
faqDetailed.a23: No. YT Playlist Cal is an independent utility. YouTube™ is a trademark of Google LLC. This tool is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with YouTube or Google in any way.
faqDetailed.q24: How can I report a bug or suggest a feature?
faqDetailed.a24: Please use the Contact page to reach us. We read every message and use feedback to prioritize improvements.

watchTimeDetail.whatP: YouTube watch time refers to the total cumulative duration you would spend watching a playlist, video, or set of videos. Unlike YouTube's own watch time metrics (which track how long viewers have spent on your channel), this tool calculates the viewer's time investment — how long it will take you to watch the content.

watchTimeDetail.f2: Adjust for playback speed (0.5× to 3×, or any custom speed)
watchTimeDetail.f3: Calculate only a range of videos (e.g. videos 10–40)
watchTimeDetail.f4: Calculate remaining watch time from where you left off
watchTimeDetail.f5: Watch planner: given daily budget, find your finish date

speed15xDetail.ctaPrompt: Use the full calculator on the homepage:
speed15xDetail.ctaHint: Paste your playlist URL → the speed is pre-set to 1.5×
speed15xDetail.savingsTitle: How Much Time Does 1.5× Speed Save?
speed15xDetail.savingsP: At 1.5× playback speed, you watch content 50% faster. This means for every 3 hours of original content, you only need 2 hours to finish it.
speed15xDetail.whoP: 1.5× speed is one of the most popular YouTube speeds among:
speed15xDetail.w1: Students — get through lecture recordings faster without losing comprehension.
speed15xDetail.w2: Online course learners — save hours on programming, design, or business courses.
speed15xDetail.w3: Podcast listeners — many podcasts work perfectly at 1.5× since speech is slower than normal reading speed.
speed15xDetail.w4: Review viewers — re-watch familiar content faster when reviewing before an exam.
speed15xDetail.whoOutro: Research on accelerated speech suggests most people can comprehend audio at up to 1.5× before comprehension begins to drop. It is generally considered the optimal balance of speed and understanding.

speed2xDetail.savingsP: At 2× speed, you save exactly 50% of the original duration — the most dramatic time saving available on YouTube natively.
speed2xDetail.whoP: 2× speed requires a higher cognitive load. It works best for:
speed2xDetail.w1: Content you're familiar with (review sessions, second watches)
speed2xDetail.w3: Tutorial content with long pauses or filler
speed2xDetail.whoOutro: For new material requiring deep comprehension, 1.25× or 1.5× is generally more effective.

remainingTimeDetail.ctaHint: Select "Remaining" mode → enter the video you watched last → calculate
remainingTimeDetail.howTitle: How to Calculate Remaining Playlist Time
remainingTimeDetail.s1: Go to your YouTube playlist and note the number of the last video you watched.
remainingTimeDetail.s2: Paste the playlist URL into YT Playlist Cal.
remainingTimeDetail.s3: Select the Remaining mode from the mode selector.
remainingTimeDetail.s4: Enter the video number you finished watching (e.g. 12) in the "I've watched through video #" field.
remainingTimeDetail.s5: Click Calculate and get the total remaining watch time plus speed-adjusted estimates.
remainingTimeDetail.whyP: YouTube playlists don't tell you how much time is left. Whether you're:
remainingTimeDetail.w1: Halfway through a 40-hour programming course and want to know how many weeks remain
remainingTimeDetail.w2: Watching a binge-worthy series with a tight schedule
remainingTimeDetail.w3: Studying before an exam and need to plan your remaining study time
remainingTimeDetail.w4: Finishing a certification course before a deadline
remainingTimeDetail.whyOutro: The Remaining Time Calculator gives you a precise figure plus a Daily Watch Planner to schedule your remaining viewing.

privacyDetail.intro: YT Playlist Cal ("we", "our", "the tool") is an independent utility website that calculates YouTube playlist lengths and watch times. This Privacy Policy explains what information we process when you use the tool, how it is used, and how we protect your privacy.
privacyDetail.s1P1Text: When you submit a YouTube URL for calculation, that URL is sent to our server, which uses it to make a request to the YouTube Data API v3. We do not store, log, or retain your YouTube URLs beyond the duration of the API request.
privacyDetail.s1P2Text: If you provide your own YouTube API key in the Advanced Options section, it is transmitted over HTTPS and used only for your specific request. We do not store, log, or transmit your API key to any third party. It is discarded after the request completes.
privacyDetail.s1P3Text: We may use privacy-conscious analytics to understand general usage patterns such as page visits, tool usage events, and geographic distribution. This data is aggregated and not tied to individual identities. We do not send YouTube URLs or API keys to analytics services.
privacyDetail.s1P4Text: We use your browser's localStorage solely to remember your dark/light mode preference and language selection. No personal data is stored in localStorage.
privacyDetail.s1P5Text: Our hosting provider (Cloudflare) may maintain server access logs including IP addresses and request timestamps as part of normal server operations. These logs are governed by Cloudflare's privacy policy. We do not add additional logging of your URLs or API keys.
privacyDetail.s2Text: YT Playlist Cal does not set cookies for tracking or advertising purposes. We use no third-party tracking cookies. If you consent to analytics, a minimal analytics script may be loaded that follows privacy-by-default principles.
privacyDetail.s3Text1: YouTube Data API v3: We use the YouTube Data API to retrieve playlist and video metadata. Your request goes through our server — we do not expose our API key to the client. YouTube's data use is governed by Google's Privacy Policy.
privacyDetail.s3Text2: Cloudflare: Our website is hosted and proxied through Cloudflare, which may process request metadata as part of its global CDN and security services.
privacyDetail.s3Text3: Font loading: We use Bunny Fonts (a GDPR-compliant alternative to Google Fonts) to load the Inter typeface. No personal data is sent to Bunny Fonts.
privacyDetail.s4Text: The website may display advertisements via Google AdSense or a comparable advertising network. Ad networks may set cookies and track behavior across websites. You can opt out of personalized advertising through Google Ad Settings.
privacyDetail.s5Text: YT Playlist Cal is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children.
privacyDetail.s6Text: Since we do not collect or store personal data beyond transient request processing, there is typically no data to access, correct, or delete. If you have a question about data we may hold, please contact us via the Contact page.
privacyDetail.s7Text: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Changes will be reflected with an updated "Last updated" date at the top of this page. Continued use of the tool after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.
privacyDetail.s8Text: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy, please use the Contact page.

disclaimerDetail.s3Text2: Discrepancies in total duration, video counts, or speed-adjusted watch times may arise due to factors beyond our control, including:
